name: AI SEO Masterclass - Module 8 Content Strategy for LLM Dominance
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-08

# Summary
"AI content is fine. AI slop without editing is not." Module 8 gives a five-phase AI content workflow, a master prompt, a freshness system, schema templates, distribution tiers, content velocity targets and a monthly quality audit.

# Five-phase workflow (time split)
1. Research and planning (30%): intent, top 10 audit, People Also Ask, real statistics, written brief.
2. AI generation (20%): section by section from the brief.
3. Human enhancement (30%): experience, fact-checking, voice, deeper analysis, visuals.
4. Optimization (10%): keyword placement, schema, internal links, metas, images, mobile.
5. Publication and distribution (10%): GSC submission, social, syndication, early links.
Tip: if human editing is under 30% of the time, the piece is likely too generic to be cited.

# Master prompt elements
Role, context (keyword, brand, type, word count, audience, year), research data, structure rules, writing style, optimization rules, prohibited elements (generic openers, keyword stuffing, unverified claims, em dashes, AI mentions). Iterate outline, intro, then sections.

# Freshness system
Monthly for high-traffic pages (date, stats, examples, links, screenshots), quarterly for medium, annual sweep for all. Show year in H1 and a "Last updated" line.

# Schema
Article (with dateModified), FAQPage, HowTo, Product, LocalBusiness. Validate before publishing; schema must match visible content exactly; update dateModified on every edit.

# Distribution pyramid and velocity
Own site, owned syndication (Medium with canonical, LinkedIn, newsletter), social (Reddit, Facebook Groups, Quora), external (guest posts, podcasts). Velocity: daily for 3 months, then 3 to 4 per week, then 2 to 3 per week. Mix: 60% listicles, 20% how-to, 10% comparisons, 10% research. 3 to 5 internal links per piece.

# Quality scorecard
Freshness, depth, uniqueness, structure, engagement scored 1 to 5 each: 22 to 25 keep, 17 to 21 refresh, 12 to 16 rewrite, under 12 delete or redirect.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Closely matches TAG rules: no em dashes, human-verified claims, FAQ schema matching visible content, keyphrase in H1 ([SEO Blog Writing Standards](lib:brain-seo-blog-writing-standards)).
- TAG cadence is set per client (Pipeliners about 1 blog per week); daily publishing is not the TAG plan.
- The scorecard is a good fit for [SEO Tracker](lib:brain-seo-tracker) update tracking and the content module of [AIO SEO CRM](lib:brain-aio-seo-crm).
